learned_patterns.pattern: The Signal Engine and scheduled sessions appear to have stopped entirely: the newest matrix is 22 days old and CLU_MEMORY.md had not been written since 06-30. The §2.5 staleness guard correctly forces SAFE MODE, but a multi-week outage means the account has run unmanaged between the automated stop monitor and ad-hoc agentic fills. Restoring the workflow scheduler is the single highest-priority fix.

A second untracked agentic fill surfaced only via broker reconciliation: INTC was stop-sold 07-07 at $109.01 with no memory written, exactly like the 06-30 JEPQ buy. Broker state is the sole source of truth (§5.1); prose memory drifts badly during an outage. Always reconcile positions AND recent orders and fold in every agentic fill.

INTC's wide 12.6% ATR stop ($112.06) still realized a -14.98% loss because price gapped straight through it — the fill printed at $109.01, below the stop level. Confirms the §3 rationale that between-session gaps are the dominant unhedged risk for fractional positions, and that wide ATR stops on high-vol single names (INTC ATR 7.64%) can be expensive when a gap does come.

An organic exit fixed the LAB overweight without any force-sell: INTC's stop-out pulled LAB from 25.9% back to 17.9% (in band), exactly the §17.3 mechanism — let stops/profit-takes reduce an overweight tier rather than trimming to rebalance. DRIP is now the most-underweight sleeve (-5.7pp) and the next-deposit target.

Signals shown here are the stale 06-30 matrix and must not be traded on. Note NVDA reads BEARISH (composite -0.338, Trend Down) on that matrix yet is the only LAB name up since — another data point that a lagging composite can misread a name right before it works. Live re-computation is required before any of these reads is actionable.
